newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Freezing rain turns Belgium into ice rink.
newsitem.headline: Freezing rain turns Belgium into ice rink.

text.p: Light rain falling on already frozen roads turned west and south Belgium into a giant ice rink on Thursday, with buses confined to depots and police reporting many crashes on the roads.
In one accident a lorry skidded off the road between Brussels and the port of Ostend, spilling a load of radio-active isotopes and causing a long tail-back.
On the ring road around Brussels traffic was moving at a crawl, with the sides of the road littered with dented vehicles.
Motorways heading south and west were not in much better shape.
Gritting lorries worked through the night trying to keep the main arteries open, but in some places they were frozen again only a few hours later.

After 17 days of sub-zero temperatures and with no respite forecast before next week, electricity consumption is soaring, gas and water mains are rupturing and the prices of root vegetables are going through the roof.
In just one week the price of a bundle of leeks has jumped from 50 francs ($1.60) to 198 francs ($6.20).
Farmers reported that in some places the ground is frozen to a depth of 40 centimetres making it impossible to harvest vegetables such as leeks without the aid of a pickaxe.
